correctness.rationale: The frozen claim is mathematically correct. The repaired RESULT.md retains the full five-vertex classification and explicitly separates it from the sharp-size corollary. Conditional on an unmonitored seed, the directional passages are independent on disjoint edges; the nearer sentinel in each direction suffices. An independent interval Markov calculation (/workspace/checks/5.py) integrated the discounted time before detection symbolically and checked all 20 placements on P₂–P₅ against the stated tails as identities in Q(z), not just at sampled transform arguments. At z=0 the exact means recover the three five-vertex minimizers with dimensionless mean 1/2 and the endpoint mean 3/5. On P₅ the three inferior reflection types are strictly dominated at all x>0. The two remaining scaled differences are 1+2x−e^x and e^x−1−2x−2x². Derivative signs give unique positive crossings, and the latter difference equals −2ξ² at ξ, so η>ξ. Comparing through the middle pair type gives the complete optimizer sets, including exactly the three placements at each tie. In the retained statement, all deadline optima minimize the mean before η, the endpoint pair joins the tied optima at η, and thereafter it alone minimizes the tail with 20% greater mean. Rate scaling uses x=λt. The companion's all-time formulas on P₂–P₄, also corroborated by the check, establish the corollary that no shorter path has a mean-suboptimal deadline optimum. No finite transform check alone proves an all-time phase diagram; the sign analysis does.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The all-path theorem covers the asymptotic endpoint phase and the very-short/very-long reversal. It does not assert where the change occurs on P₅, whether one or several changes occur, or which nonendpoint placements are ever optimal. General optimization objectives and guarantees provide no such exact breakpoints.

evidence: Equation (1) gives dimensionless mean 3/5 at P₅ endpoints and 1/2 at {1,3}; the companion theorem already makes the first pair uniquely optimal at sufficiently long finite deadlines. The companion analysis does not include the P₅ comparison e^x−1−2x−2x², which determines the second crossing against the reflected intermediate optimizer class.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The sharp threshold n=5 follows mechanically from those theorem statements and the two direct mean integrals, without knowing the P₅ phase diagram. The full repair requires an additional exponential-polynomial envelope analysis: eliminate three pair types, exhibit the intermediate optimizer with reflection, order the two distinct positive roots, and resolve the two ties. That exact information is not a specialization of the broader early/late optimizer theorem; the unoptimized tail formula is a starting point, not an optimized result.
